question: Under S.C. Code Section 50-21-110, what is an explicit example of "negligent operation" of a vessel?
choice_a: Operating a water device at more than idle speed within a designated no-wake zone
choice_b: Anchoring in open water away from other traffic
choice_c: Wearing a properly fitted PFD at all times
choice_d: Displaying working navigation lights at night
explanation: Section 50-21-110 identifies operating a water device at more than idle speed within a no-wake zone as a specific example of negligent operation, alongside more generally operating too fast for existing conditions, distinguishing this lesser offense from the willful-or-wanton standard required for reckless operation.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-110 (negligent operation, no-wake-zone speed example)

question: What is the penalty range for a negligent operation conviction under Section 50-21-110?
choice_a: A fine of $50 to $200 or up to 30 days imprisonment
choice_b: A mandatory minimum of one year in prison with no fine option
choice_c: No penalty at all; negligent operation is not a punishable offense
choice_d: A flat $10,000 fine regardless of circumstances
explanation: Section 50-21-110 sets a negligent operation penalty of a $50 to $200 fine or up to 30 days imprisonment, a lower range than reckless operation under Section 50-21-111, reflecting negligent operation's lesser culpability standard.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-110 (negligent operation penalty)

question: Under Section 50-21-110, what happens if a South Carolina boater accumulates three negligent operation convictions within a five-year period?
choice_a: Nothing beyond the fine for the third conviction
choice_b: The boater must complete an approved boating safety program at their own expense and their boating privileges are suspended until that course is completed
choice_c: Their vessel is permanently confiscated with no possibility of return
choice_d: All prior convictions are automatically erased
explanation: Section 50-21-110 imposes an added consequence for repeat negligent operators: three convictions within five years triggers a mandatory boating safety course, paid for by the violator, with boating privileges suspended until the course is successfully completed.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-110 (mandatory course after three negligent-operation convictions in five years)

question: Under S.C. Code Section 50-21-113, what penalty applies to a boating-under-the-influence violation that causes great bodily injury to another person?
choice_a: A misdemeanor with a $50 fine and no possibility of imprisonment
choice_b: A felony with a $5,000 to $10,000 fine and imprisonment of 30 days to 15 years
choice_c: No specific penalty is defined for causing injury
choice_d: A civil fine only, with the matter never going through criminal court
explanation: Section 50-21-113 elevates the offense sharply when impaired boat operation causes great bodily injury, making it a felony punishable by a $5,000 to $10,000 fine and imprisonment ranging from 30 days to 15 years, well beyond the penalties for ordinary BUI under Section 50-21-112.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-113 (BUI resulting in great bodily injury)

question: Under Section 50-21-113, what penalty applies when boating under the influence results in another person's death?
choice_a: A felony with a $10,000 to $25,000 fine and imprisonment of 1 to 25 years
choice_b: The same misdemeanor penalty as a first-offense BUI with no injury
choice_c: There is no distinct penalty for a death resulting from BUI beyond the standard first-offense fine
choice_d: A fine only, with imprisonment never authorized regardless of the facts
explanation: Section 50-21-113 makes a BUI violation that results in death a felony carrying a $10,000 to $25,000 fine and imprisonment of 1 to 25 years, reflecting the most serious tier of South Carolina's impaired-boating penalty structure.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-113 (BUI resulting in death)

question: Under S.C. Code Section 50-21-114, what does simply operating a vessel on South Carolina's waters mean a person has already agreed to, if later arrested on a BUI-related charge?
choice_a: Nothing; a separate written consent form must be signed before any testing can ever occur
choice_b: Implied consent to a chemical test or analysis of the person's breath, blood, or urine to determine alcohol or drug content
choice_c: Automatic conviction with no right to contest the charge
choice_d: Consent applies only to a breathalyzer and never to a blood or urine test under any circumstance
explanation: Section 50-21-114 establishes that operating a vessel on South Carolina's waters constitutes implied consent to a chemical test of breath, blood, or urine if the operator is later arrested for a BUI-related offense, mirroring the implied consent framework used for impaired driving on the road.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-114 (implied consent to chemical testing)

question: Under Section 50-21-114, what consequence follows if a boater refuses to submit to a properly requested chemical test after a BUI-related arrest?
choice_a: There is no consequence for refusing a chemical test
choice_b: A 180-day suspension of boating privileges, effective the day after notice unless a hearing is timely requested
choice_c: Refusal automatically results in acquittal of any related charge
choice_d: A refusal simply delays testing with no suspension consequence at all
explanation: Section 50-21-114 imposes a 180-day suspension of boating privileges for refusing a properly requested chemical test, effective the day after notice unless the person timely requests a hearing to contest it, creating a strong incentive to comply with lawfully requested testing.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-114 (180-day suspension for refusing chemical testing)

question: Under S.C. Code Section 50-21-115, what is "reckless homicide by operation of a boat"?
choice_a: Any accident resulting only in property damage, regardless of injury
choice_b: A death occurring within three years as the proximate result of an injury caused by operating a boat in reckless disregard of the safety of others
choice_c: A term with no legal definition in South Carolina's boating chapter
choice_d: Any death that occurs on a boat regardless of cause, including natural causes
explanation: Section 50-21-115 defines reckless homicide by boat operation as a death occurring within three years as the proximate result of an injury inflicted by operating a boat in reckless disregard of others' safety, tying the timing of the death to the original reckless act.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-115 (reckless homicide by boat operation, definition)

question: Under Section 50-21-115, besides a fine and imprisonment, what additional consequence may a court impose after a conviction for reckless homicide, involuntary manslaughter, manslaughter, or murder involving a boat?
choice_a: The court has no authority to restrict future boat operation under any circumstance
choice_b: The court may prohibit the person from operating any boat for up to five years following the conviction
choice_c: The court may only suspend privileges for 48 hours
choice_d: The court must permanently and irrevocably revoke the person's driver's license for unrelated highway driving
explanation: Section 50-21-115 gives the court discretion to prohibit a person convicted of reckless homicide, involuntary manslaughter, manslaughter, or murder involving a boat from operating any boat for up to five years after the conviction, on top of any fine or imprisonment imposed.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-115 (up to five-year boat-operation prohibition after conviction)

question: Under S.C. Code Section 50-21-117, what is the penalty for a first violation of operating a vessel while boating privileges are suspended?
choice_a: A fine of $200 or up to 30 days imprisonment
choice_b: Automatic permanent revocation with no fine option
choice_c: No penalty, since a suspension alone is considered sufficient
choice_d: A mandatory 5-year prison sentence with no fine option
explanation: Section 50-21-117 penalizes a first offense of operating while boating privileges are suspended with a $200 fine or up to 30 days imprisonment, with penalties escalating substantially for second and subsequent violations, including additional suspension time added by the department.
source_note: S.C. Code Ann. Section 50-21-117 (penalty for operating while privileges are suspended)
